{{short description|Result in algebraic topology}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Stallings–Zeeman theorem''' is a result in [[algebraic topology]], used in the proof of the [[Poincaré conjecture]] for [[dimension]] greater than or equal to five. It is named after the [[mathematician]]s [[John R. Stallings]] and [[Christopher Zeeman]].

==Statement of the theorem==
Let ''M'' be a finite [[simplicial complex]] of dimension dim(''M'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;5. Suppose that ''M'' has the [[homotopy type]] of the ''m''-dimensional [[sphere]] '''S'''<sup>''m''</sup> and that ''M'' is locally [[piecewise linear function|piecewise linearly]] [[homeomorphism|homeomorphic]] to ''m''-dimensional [[Euclidean space]] '''R'''<sup>''m''</sup>. Then ''M'' is homeomorphic to '''S'''<sup>''m''</sup> under a map that is piecewise linear except possibly at a single point ''x''. That is, ''M''&nbsp;\&nbsp;{''x''} is piecewise linearly homeomorphic to '''R'''<sup>''m''</sup>.
